claim_scope: Compare a compact four-summand S3 solver on exact window-orbit bases with the archived Q1480 weight-base solver on the same N53/N83 ordinary public targets. Pinned and unpinned planted controls check correctness only. Successful ordinary work, natural yield, and N131 2^x remain unknown until measured.

point_decomposition.equations: The same balanced three-S3 chain used by Q1480, with the first pair handled by exact native S3 root theory and the final and right links in the compact CNF.
point_decomposition.leaf_constraint: At least one cyclic window selector per leaf; each selected window forces every coordinate outside its d positions to zero; each leaf is nonzero. No cardinality network is needed.
point_decomposition.theory_weight_parameter: The native solver receives d as a Hamming-weight upper bound. Every window-valid leaf has weight <= d, so every sound rejection for the larger weight<=d domain remains sound for the window subset. This may be weak and is not a measured speed claim.
point_decomposition.solver_binary: Q1480 frozen native conditioned-join solver, reused without source changes

planted_control_rule: In Q1481 representative order, select the first four rational raw x orbits whose cofactor-projected keys are distinct. Use curve.pointFromX's deterministic sign. Their raw sum defines the one raw target x; their cofactor-projected sum defines the public target. If the sum is identity, continue to the next distinct orbit until nonidentity. This is fixture construction outside the target-dependent interval and never estimates ordinary yield.
success_gates: Both pinned controls return independently verified four-distinct-column public relations.
Every ordinary run preserves a raw status, all failed/censored attempts, exact SAT and field operation counters, wall interval, and peak RSS.
A verified unpinned N83 ordinary relation is required before claiming successful N83 decomposition work or fitting a N131 growth law.
